question: A woman requests TOLAC (Trial of Labour After Caesarean) for her second pregnancy. Which previous uterine incision type is an absolute contraindication to TOLAC regardless of other favourable factors?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A previous LSCS (lower segment transverse) incision is the ONLY scar type suitable for TOLAC. It heals well and carries a low uterine rupture risk (~0.5–0.9%).

Correct. A previous classical (upper segment vertical) incision is an absolute contraindication to TOLAC. The risk of uterine rupture is 4–9% — far higher than with an LSCS scar — and rupture can be catastrophic and sudden.

While prior uterine rupture significantly increases recurrence risk and makes TOLAC inadvisable, it is generally listed among the major contraindications alongside classical incision in most guidelines.

answers.text: Low vertical (De Lee) incision extending into the lower segment only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A low vertical incision confined to the lower segment carries somewhat higher risk than LSCS but is not universally classified as an absolute contraindication; it is managed on a case-by-case basis by most guidelines.

overallFeedback.feedback: Classical (upper segment vertical) caesarean incision is the key absolute contraindication to TOLAC. Always establish the scar type before any TOLAC discussion.
Correct. Classical (upper segment) scar = absolute contraindication to TOLAC. The scar type overrides all other eligibility factors.
